body_markdown:
When it made its debut earlier in 2026,[the Aston Martin Dreadnought](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/aston-martin-dreadnought-call-of-duty-pictures-specs/) was presented as a virtual concept designed for *Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4* . It’s about to exit the digital world and land in one of the most unforgiving races on the planet. Aston Martin Racing has announced that it will compete in[the Dakar Rally](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/the-dakar-rally-is-for-the-racers-not-the-fans/) for the first time with three examples of the Dreadnought.


Aston Martin developed the Dakar-bound Dreadnought with the help of Prodrive, a race engineering company that has worked closely with the British brand’s endurance racing team for over 20 years. Don’t look for[DBX](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/aston-martin-dbx-s-pictures-specs/) underpinnings here: The off-roader is a true, purpose-designed rally car that shares nothing with Aston Martin’s production models. The renderings released by the firm show a buggy-like racer with huge tires, a generous amount of ground clearance, and extreme approach and departure angles.

The styling evolved considerably as the Dreadnought made the leap from your monitor to the dunes. While the original concept almost reminded us of classic Aston Martin models, the rally car headed to Dakar is characterized by a function-over-form design drawn around off-road capability, cooling, and aerodynamics. Only the shape of the hood and the rear spoiler hint that it’s an Aston.


Specifications haven’t been released, though it looks like the Dreadnought is powered by a mid-mounted engine. It takes more than raw power to win Dakar, however, so Aston Martin has recruited a star-studded lineup of drivers for the race. One car will be given to Fernando Alonso, who currently drives for Aston Martin’s Formula 1 team. He’s a two-time Formula 1 world champion, and he won the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2018 and 2019. Another will be driven by nine-time WRC winner Sébastien Loeb, while the third will be in the hands of reigning FIA World Rally Raid champion Lucas Moraes. All three pilots have previously raced in the Dakar.


The 2027 Dakar Rally will take place from January 9 to 23. It starts in the south of Portugal, heads across southern Spain, and goes into Morocco, where most of the race takes place. This will be the first time that the Dakar Rally is held in Africa since 2007, and[the route](https://www.dakar.com/en/overall-route) sounds like a tough one. It includes over 2600 miles of special stages through the Atlas Mountains and the Sahara Desert.
